output.rootCause: CHG-402 reduced the Redis client pool from 80 to 8 and queueTimeoutMs from a safe value to 250ms, causing IdempotencyStore lookups to time out (LOG-10A: 'timeout after 3000ms; retrying request') and POST /orders latency/errors to spike. Retried requests then hit createOrder(), which is not actually idempotent: it never checks whether idempotencyKey already exists, so each retry inserts a new order, producing duplicate orders and failing the idempotency regression test.
evidence: CHG-402: redis.client.poolSize reduced from 80 to 8; current src/redisPool.js shows poolSize:8 and queueTimeoutMs:250, below test thresholds of >=64 and >=800
LOG-10A: 'IdempotencyStore timeout after 3000ms; retrying request' indicates pool starvation/queue timeout during idempotency lookup
METRIC-55: POST /orders p95 rose from 420ms to 2.8s and error rate from 0.2% to 7.4%, consistent with exhausted Redis pool and retries
test/redisPool.test.js fails: 'connection pool preserves checkout peak capacity' expects poolSize >=64 and 'queue timeout absorbs short checkout bursts' expects queueTimeoutMs >=800

src/order.js createOrder() always creates and overwrites ordersByKey; duplicate request does not check existing key and returns a new 201 order instead of 409 with original order, causing duplicate orders on retry

test/order.test.js 'duplicate request returns the original order without creating another' expects status 409 and same order.id, but current implementation would return 201 and ORD-2; CI baseline is red on both connection-pool and idempotency tests
output.fixPlan: 1) Revert redisPoolConfig to match pre-CHG-402 capacity: set poolSize back to >=80 (at least satisfy test >=64) and queueTimeoutMs >=800 (or restore original 3000ms timeout) to prevent IdempotencyStore timeouts. 2) Fix createOrder idempotency: at the start, if ordersByKey.has(idempotencyKey), return { status: 409, order: ordersByKey.get(idempotencyKey) }; only create and store a new order when the key is absent. 3) Ensure the payment/order retry path treats 409 as a successful idempotent replay and does not surface it as an error. 4) Add regression tests for duplicate idempotencyKey returning the original order and for pool size/queue timeout meeting peak capacity expectations. 5) Run CI until main is green, then redeploy the fixed release; consider adding Redis pool saturation alerts to catch future pool-size regressions.

modelCalls.patchSummary: Restore Redis pool capacity and queue timeout to prevent checkout peak starvation, and make createOrder idempotent by returning 409 with the original order when the idempotencyKey already exists.
modelCalls.patchRollback: Run `git revert <commit>` for the CHG-402 change and redeploy the last known-good build. For emergency rollback, set redisPoolConfig.poolSize=80 and queueTimeoutMs=3000, and restore the previous createOrder implementation with duplicate-key 409 handling.
